claims.summary: On a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a finite field, genus g, n distinct rational evaluation points, divisors A,G of nonnegative degrees a,m avoiding those points, t>=0, a>=t+g and n>a+m+t, recover any f in L(G) from its evaluations corrupted at <=t unknown positions. Solve N(P_i)=lambda(P_i)y_i with lambda in L(A), N in L(A+G). Nonzero solutions exist, every nonzero solution has lambda nonzero and N=lambda f identically, and kills every actual error. A second weighted evaluation system uniquely recovers f. If rational R avoids the points and supports of A,G and a>=t+2g, add lambda(R)=1; the system remains consistent and N(R)=f(R). With bases/evaluation matrices supplied, O(n^3) field operations and O(n^2) memory. Costs of producing those inputs are separate. This supplies geometric certificates for established bilinear error recovery, not a new decoder or a bounded-PC identification.

claims.summary: For every s=2^r>=4 in a supplied field F_(s^2), use the Hermitian curve Y^s Z+YZ^s=X^(s+1), infinity P=(0:1:0), protected R=(0:0:1), and all affine rational points except R. Set n=s^3-1,g=s(s-1)/2,m=s^3/4-1,t=s^3/8-1,a=t+2g,G=mP,A=aP. Marked curve recovery corrects every error pattern of size<=t and returns lambda(R)=1, preserving the message value there. Dimension is m-g+1. Bases L(bP) are x^i y^j for i>=0,0<=j<s and si+(s+1)j<=b. Points, bases, evaluation matrices and decoding use O(n^3) field operations/O(n^2) storage. Field construction excluded; pole filtration is not total polynomial degree. Positive genus and length are unbounded; no new code, radius improvement or binary-PC transfer claimed.
